title: Grade 8 Science — Wed, Jun 11
description: Metals and Non-metals — Day 3 of 5: Reactivity series and displacement reactions
subject: science

questions.question: The reactivity series arranges metals in order of their:
questions.explanation: The reactivity series lists metals from most reactive (potassium) to least reactive (gold), based on their tendency to react.

questions.question: In the reactivity series, which metal is the MOST reactive?
questions.explanation: Potassium (K) is the most reactive common metal. It reacts explosively with cold water.

questions.question: Which metal is the LEAST reactive in the common reactivity series?
questions.explanation: Gold is the least reactive metal. It does not tarnish, corrode, or react with most chemicals — hence used in jewellery.

questions.question: A displacement reaction occurs when a more reactive metal:
options: Replaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution
questions.explanation: A more reactive metal displaces (pushes out) a less reactive metal from its compound in solution.

questions.question: When iron is dipped in copper sulphate solution, the solution turns from blue to light green because:
options: Iron dissolves and copper sulphate becomes stronger
Iron displaces copper; copper deposits on iron; iron sulphate (light green) forms
Copper becomes more reactive than iron
questions.explanation: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. Iron (more reactive) displaces copper. Iron sulphate is light green; copper metal deposits on the iron.

questions.question: Will copper displace zinc from zinc sulphate solution?
options: No, because copper is less reactive than zinc
questions.explanation: Copper is below zinc in the reactivity series (less reactive). A less reactive metal cannot displace a more reactive one.

questions.question: Thermite reaction uses aluminium to displace iron from iron oxide because:
options: Aluminium is below iron in the reactivity series
Aluminium is more reactive than iron and displaces it
Iron is more expensive than aluminium
questions.explanation: Al is above Fe in the reactivity series. The thermite reaction: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe, releasing intense heat.

questions.question: Arrange these metals from most reactive to least reactive: Gold, Zinc, Iron, Copper
questions.explanation: The correct reactivity order (most → least): Zinc > Iron > Copper > Gold. Zinc displaces iron, which displaces copper.

questions.question: Which of these metals reacts with cold water to give hydrogen gas?
questions.explanation: Sodium (Na) is highly reactive and reacts vigorously with cold water: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂↑.

questions.question: Iron reacts with steam (but not cold water) to give:
questions.explanation: 3Fe + 4H₂O(steam) → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂. Iron reacts with steam to form iron oxide (magnetite) and hydrogen gas.

questions.question: The reactivity series is useful for predicting whether a:
options: Metal has a high boiling point
Displacement reaction will occur between a metal and a salt solution
questions.explanation: The reactivity series tells us which metal can displace another from its salt solution — a very practical prediction tool.

questions.question: Silver is below copper in the reactivity series. This means silver:
options: Reacts faster than copper with acids
Cannot displace copper from copper sulphate solution
questions.explanation: Since silver is below copper (less reactive), it cannot displace copper from its salt solution.

questions.question: When zinc granules are added to dilute sulphuric acid, bubbles are seen because:
options: Hydrogen gas is released — Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑
questions.explanation: Zinc displaces hydrogen from sulphuric acid. The bubbles seen are hydrogen gas being released.

questions.question: Which of these pairs would result in a displacement reaction?
options: Copper added to zinc sulphate solution
Zinc added to copper sulphate solution
Gold added to iron sulphate solution
Silver added to potassium chloride solution
questions.explanation: Zinc (more reactive) displaces copper (less reactive) from copper sulphate: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.

questions.question: In the reactivity series, hydrogen is also included. A metal above hydrogen in the series:
options: Can displace hydrogen from dilute acids
questions.explanation: Metals above hydrogen (like zinc, iron, magnesium) displace hydrogen from dilute acids. Metals below hydrogen (copper, silver, gold) do not.
